text: Mezue ilu a ma ama: “Egbe bere, … bere; nke sị ibe ya ebela, nku kwaa ya.”
gloss: Complete the famous proverb: 'Let the kite perch, let ___ perch; whichever says the other shall not, may its wing break.' — Ugo (eagle): «Egbe bere, ugo bere», the Igbo proverb of live and let live.

text: Ndị Igbo kwenyere na mmadụ ọ bụla nwere onye nche mmụọ nke ya. Mezue ilu a: “Onye kwe, … ya ekwe.”
gloss: Igbo believe every person has their own spiritual guardian. Complete: 'If a person agrees, his ___ agrees.' — Chi: «Onye kwe, chi ya ekwe», the personal chi.

text: Àkwà mmiri a ma ama jikọrọ Ọnịcha na Asaba. Kedu osimiri ọ gafere?
gloss: The famous bridge links Onitsha and Asaba. Which river does it cross? — The Niger: the Niger Bridge (1965) spans it between Anambra and Delta.

text: Kedu akụkụ ahụ na-agba ọbara gaa n'akụkụ ahụ mmadụ niile, ehihie na abalị?
gloss: Which organ pumps blood to every part of the body, day and night? — The heart (obi); the others are lungs, liver, kidney.

text: N'ogige, e nwere ọkụkọ atọ na ewu abụọ. Ụkwụ ole ka ha niile nwere?
gloss: In a yard there are three hens and two goats. How many legs in all? — 14: 3×2 + 2×4. 10 and 20 catch those who give every animal the same number of legs.

text: Kedu agba ọkụ okporo ụzọ na-agwa ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala ka ha kwụsị?
gloss: Which traffic-light colour tells drivers to stop? — Red.

text: Kedu ihe ọkụkụ a na-esi na ya emepụta abacha, nke a na-agwakọta na ụgba na mmanụ nkwụ?
gloss: From which crop is abacha made, the dish mixed with ugba and palm oil? — Cassava (akpụ): abacha is boiled, shredded and dried cassava.

text: Ada lakpuru ụra n'elekere iri nke abalị, hie ụra awa asatọ zuru oke. Kedu elekere o tetara n'ụtụtụ?
gloss: Ada went to bed at 10 p.m. and slept a full eight hours. What time did she wake? — 6 a.m.; 'eight o'clock' is the trap for those who repeat the number of hours.

text: N'akụkọ ifo ndị Igbo, kedu anụmanụ a ma ama maka aghụghọ ya, nke na-aghọgbu ụmụ anụmanụ ibe ya oge niile?
gloss: In Igbo folktales, which animal is famous for its cunning, always tricking the other animals? — The tortoise (mbe), the trickster of Igbo folklore.

text: Simba, dike nke ihe nkiri katuun Disney nke afọ 1994, bụ nwa anụmanụ ole?
gloss: Simba, hero of Disney's 1994 cartoon, is the cub of which animal? — A lion (ọdụm), from The Lion King; 'simba' is Swahili for lion.

text: Kedu ọnụ ọgụgụ kachasị ukwuu n'ime ndị a?
gloss: Which of these numbers is the largest? — Iri atọ (30). The others are 29, 19 and 28: the big unit 'itoolu' (9) tempts the eye.

text: N'Igbo, a na-akpọ ebe anyanwụ na-ada “ọdịda anyanwụ”. Ọ bụrụ na i chee ihu n'ebe ahụ, kedu akụkụ ga-adị n'aka nri gị?
gloss: In Igbo, where the sun sets is 'ọdịda anyanwụ' (west). Facing that way, which direction is on your right? — Ugwu (north).

text: Otu okwu Igbo, dabere n'ụda e ji akpọ ya, pụtara ihe ọkụkọ na-eyi, ihe e ji ekpuchi ahụ, ihe a na-edina n'elu ya ehi ụra, na ihe nwa na-eme mgbe agụụ na-agụ ya. Kedu okwu ahụ?
gloss: One Igbo word, depending on its tones, means what a hen lays, what covers the body, what you lie on to sleep, and what a hungry baby does. Which? — Akwa: àkwá (egg), ákwà (cloth), àkwà (bed), ákwá (crying). The classic example of Igbo tone.

text: N'ime steeti ise dị na Ndịda Ọwụwa Anyanwụ Naịjirịa, naanị otu nwere isi obodo nke aha ya na aha steeti ahụ bụ otu. Kedu isi obodo ahụ?
gloss: Of the five South-East states, only one has a capital with the same name as the state. Which capital? — Enugu. Owerri (Imo), Umuahia (Abia), Abakaliki (Ebonyi) and Awka (Anambra) all differ.

text: Ọtụtụ ndị Naịjirịa na-akpọ onye nkiri ọchị Nkem Owoh aha agwa ama ama o mere. Kedu aha ahụ?
gloss: Many Nigerians call the comic actor Nkem Owoh by the name of his famous character. Which? — Osuofia. Mr Ibu is John Okafor; Aki and Pawpaw are Chinedu Ikedieze and Osita Iheme.

text: Kedu ngwa egwu Igbo a kpụrụ n'ụrọ, nke onye na-akpọ ya na-eji aka akụ oghere dị n'akụkụ ya ka o nye ụda dị omimi?
gloss: Which Igbo instrument is moulded from clay, the player striking a hole in its side for a deep sound? — Udu, the clay pot drum. Ogene is a metal gong, ekwe a wooden slit drum, ọja a flute.

text: A kụrụ osisi ise n'otu ahịrị, nke ọ bụla dị mita abụọ site n'ibe ya. Ogologo ole dị n'etiti osisi nke mbụ na nke ikpeazụ?
gloss: Five trees are planted in a row, each two metres from the next. How far is the first from the last? — 8 m: five trees leave only four gaps. 10 m is the autopilot answer.

text: N'asọmpi bọọlụ, mmeri na-enye akara atọ, egwuregwu e gbara nhata na-enye otu akara. Otu ìgwè gbara egwuregwu ise: o meriri abụọ, gbaa nhata abụọ, e merie ya otu. Akara ole ka o nwetara?
gloss: In a football league a win gives three points, a draw one. A team played five: won two, drew two, lost one. How many points? — 8: 2×3 + 2×1 + 0.

text: Aha ihe ọṅụṅụ Coca-Cola sitere n'ihe ọkụkụ abụọ: akwụkwọ koka, na otu mkpụrụ onye Igbo ọ bụla maara nke ọma. Kedu mkpụrụ ahụ?
gloss: Coca-Cola is named after two plants: coca leaves and a nut every Igbo knows well. Which? — The kola nut (ọjị), the drink's original source of caffeine. 'Cola' ≈ kola is the step of thinking.

text: N'ime ihe ndị a na-efe efe, kedu nke na-enye ụmụ ya ara, ya bụ na ọ bụghị nnụnụ?
gloss: Of these flying creatures, which suckles its young, so is not a bird? — The bat (ụsụ), a mammal. Vulture, kite and eagle are birds.

text: Taa bụ ụbọchị ahịa ndị Igbo na-akpọ nwa nwoke a mụrụ na ya “Okoye”. Kedu ụbọchị ahịa ga-abụ echi?
gloss: Today is the market day after which a boy born on it is named 'Okoye'. What market day is tomorrow? — Afọ. Okoye is born on Oye/Orie, and the week runs Eke, Orie, Afọ, Nkwọ. Orie (today) is the trap.

text: Ndị Igbo oge gboo ji iri abụọ agụ ọnụ: otu ọgụ bụ iri abụọ, otu nnụ bụkwa ọgụ iri abụọ. Ole ka otu nnụ ruru?
gloss: Igbo traditionally counted in twenties: one ọgụ is twenty, and one nnụ is twenty ọgụ. How much is one nnụ? — 400 (20×20). 200 is the trap for those who multiply by ten.

text: Nnamdi Azikiwe tọrọ ntọala mahadum mepere ụzọ ya n'afọ 1960. N'obodo ole ka mahadum ahụ dị?
gloss: Nnamdi Azikiwe founded a university that opened its doors in 1960. In which town is it? — Nsukka: the University of Nigeria. Awka is the trap: Nnamdi Azikiwe University there is only named after him.

text: I hụrụ àmụ̀mà; sekọnd itoolu gachara, ị nụrụ égbè eluigwe ya. Ihe dị ka kilomita ole ka àmụ̀mà ahụ dị site n'ebe ị nọ?
gloss: You see lightning and hear its thunder nine seconds later. About how far away was it? — About 3 km: sound travels about 340 m per second, roughly 1 km every 3 seconds.

text: Ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa ka e nye onye ọrịa ọbara ngwa ngwa, tupu a mata ụdị ọbara ya, kedu ụdị ọbara ndị dọkịta na-enye?
gloss: If a patient needs blood urgently, before their group is known, which group do doctors give? — O negative, the universal red-cell donor. AB+ is the trap: it is the universal recipient.

text: N'ime anụmanụ ndị a, kedu nke nne ya na-adị ime ogologo oge karịa — ihe fọrọ nke nta ka ọ bụrụ afọ abụọ?
gloss: Of these animals, whose mother is pregnant longest, nearly two years? — The elephant (about 22 months). Horse about 11, cow about 9, lion under 4.

text: E dere otu ozi ahụ ugboro atọ n'ụdị ide dị iche iche na Nkume Rosetta. Kedu ide ochie nke o nyere ndị ọkà mmụta aka ịgụ?
gloss: The Rosetta Stone carries the same text three times in different scripts. Which ancient writing did it help scholars read? — Egyptian hieroglyphs (alongside Demotic and Greek).

text: Ebee ka Ibini Ukpabi dị — ebe ịgba afa a ma ama nke ndị Bekee kpọrọ “Long Juju”?
gloss: Where is Ibini Ukpabi, the famous oracle the British called the 'Long Juju'? — Arochukwu, in today's Abia State.

text: Igbo gbaziri ọtụtụ okwu n'asụsụ Bekee. Kedu okwu n'ime ndị a na-abụghị okwu e si n'asụsụ Bekee nweta?
gloss: Igbo has borrowed many words from English. Which of these is not one of them? — Ụgbọ (vessel, canoe: ụgbọ mmiri, ụgbọ ala), a native word. Tebụl, windo and kọmputa are table, window, computer.

text: Kedu mba Ugwu Kilimanjaro dị n'ime ya?
gloss: Which country is Mount Kilimanjaro in? — Tanzania. Kenya is the trap: its most famous views are from Kenya's Amboseli, across the border.

text: Kedu onye ode akwụkwọ si Oguta dere akwụkwọ akụkọ “Efuru”, nke e bipụtara n'afọ 1966?
gloss: Which writer from Oguta wrote the novel 'Efuru', published in 1966? — Flora Nwapa. All options are Igbo women novelists.

text: A na-akpọ ọla bronze ochie a gwupụtara n'Anambra, nke ndị ọkà mmụta kwuru na e mere ihe dị ka narị afọ nke itoolu, aha obodo ebe a hụrụ ha. Kedu obodo ahụ?
gloss: Ancient bronzes dug up in Anambra, dated by scholars to about the 9th century, are named after the town where they were found. Which? — Igbo-Ukwu. Nri is the trap: the finds are linked to Nri culture but named after Igbo-Ukwu.

text: Kedu ihe nkiri asụsụ Igbo nke afọ 1992 ọtụtụ mmadụ na-ewere dị ka nke malitere Nollywood?
gloss: Which 1992 Igbo-language film do many regard as the start of Nollywood? — Living in Bondage. Glamour Girls (1994), Rattlesnake (1995) and Igodo (1999) came later.

text: Kemgbe ọtụtụ narị afọ, ndị Uburu na Okposi na-esi nnu n'ọdọ mmiri nnu dị n'ala ha. Steeti ole ka obodo abụọ a dị?
gloss: For centuries the people of Uburu and Okposi have made salt from the salt lakes on their land. Which state are these two towns in? — Ebonyi (Ohaozara area).

text: Obi mmadụ toro eto nọ n'ezumike na-akụ ihe dị ka ugboro ole n'otu ụbọchị?
gloss: About how many times does a resting adult heart beat in one day? — About 100,000: roughly 70 a minute × 60 × 24 ≈ 100,800. Knowing the pulse rate and multiplying is the step.

text: Ọtụtụ mkpụrụ ndụ dị n'ahụ mmadụ nwere kromosom n'ụzọ abụọ abụọ. Kromosom ole ka mkpụrụ akwa nwanyị nwere?
gloss: Most human body cells carry their chromosomes in pairs. How many chromosomes does a human egg cell have? — 23: body cells have 23 pairs (46), and an egg carries one of each pair.

text: N'ime kọmputa, bit ọ bụla bụ 0 ma ọ bụ 1. Ụkpụrụ dị iche iche ole ka otu byte nwere ike igosi?
gloss: In a computer each bit is 0 or 1. How many different values can one byte show? — 256: a byte is 8 bits, and 2⁸ = 256. 8 is the trap for those who stop at the number of bits.

text: Angélique Kidjo, onye nwetara ihe nrite Grammy ọtụtụ ugboro, si na mba ole n'Afrịka?
gloss: Angélique Kidjo, winner of several Grammys, comes from which African country? — Benin (born in Ouidah). Togo, its neighbour, is the trap.

text: Hakeem Olajuwon, onye a mụrụ na Legọs, meriri asọmpi NBA ugboro abụọ n'ìgwè ole?
gloss: Lagos-born Hakeem Olajuwon won the NBA title twice with which team? — The Houston Rockets (1994 and 1995).

text: Mansa Musa, onye njem ya gaa Mecca n'afọ 1324 mere ka ụwa mara akụ na ụba ya, chịrị alaeze ole?
gloss: Mansa Musa, whose 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca showed the world his wealth, ruled which empire? — The Mali Empire. Songhai, ancient Ghana and Kanem-Bornu were its West African neighbours in time and place.

text: Kedu onye dere “Omenuko” (1933), nke a na-akpọ akwụkwọ akụkọ ogologo mbụ e dere n'asụsụ Igbo?
gloss: Who wrote 'Omenuko' (1933), called the first full-length novel written in Igbo? — Pita Nwana. The others are later pioneers of Igbo writing (Bell-Gam wrote 'Ije Odumodu Jere').

text: Chinua Achebe si n'ahịrị uri nke W. B. Yeats nweta aha akwụkwọ ya “Things Fall Apart”. Kedu uri ahụ?
gloss: Chinua Achebe took the title 'Things Fall Apart' from a line by W. B. Yeats. Which poem? — 'The Second Coming' ('Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold'), quoted as the novel's epigraph. All options are Yeats poems.

text: Kedu onye na-ese ihe sere “Tutu” (1974), ihe osise ọtụtụ na-akpọ “Mona Lisa nke Afrịka”?
gloss: Which painter made 'Tutu' (1974), the portrait many call the 'African Mona Lisa'? — Ben Enwonwu of Onitsha. The others are major artists linked to Nigerian modernism and Nsukka.

text: N'ime isi obodo mba ndị a, kedu nke kacha nso n'ahịrị dị n'etiti ụwa, nke kewara ya n'akụkụ ugwu na akụkụ ndịda?
gloss: Of these capitals, which is closest to the equator, the line dividing the globe into north and south? — Kampala (about 0.3° N). Nairobi is about 1.3° S, Accra 5.6° N, Abuja 9° N. Players must place each city, then compare.

text: Aha mba Argentina sitere n'okwu Latin maka otu ọla dị oke ọnụ ahịa. Kedu akara kemistri nke ọla ahụ?
gloss: Argentina's name comes from the Latin word for a precious metal. What is that metal's chemical symbol? — Ag: argentum, silver. Ar (argon) traps those matching letters; Au (gold) those guessing the most precious metal.

text: Magellan nwụrụ n'etiti njem mbụ gbara ụwa gburugburu (1519–1522). Kedu onye duru ụgbọ mmiri fọdụrụ laghachi Spen?
gloss: Magellan died midway through the first voyage around the world (1519–1522). Who led the surviving ship back to Spain? — Juan Sebastián Elcano, on the Victoria. Drake sailed round the world later, in 1577–1580.

text: Ọtụtụ mmadụ chere na okwu “emoji” sitere n'okwu Bekee “emotion”, mana o si n'asụsụ ọzọ. Kedu asụsụ ahụ?
gloss: Many think 'emoji' comes from English 'emotion', but it comes from another language. Which? — Japanese: e (picture) + moji (character). The likeness to 'emotion' is a coincidence.

text: Aha nri jollof, nke ndị Naịjirịa na ndị Ghana na-arụrịta ụka maka ya, sitere n'aha alaeze ochie nke ndị Wolof. N'ime mba ole ka alaeze ahụ dị?
gloss: The name of jollof rice, which Nigerians and Ghanaians argue over, comes from the old Wolof kingdom. In which country was it? — Senegal: the Jolof Empire. Ghana is the trap, from the jollof rivalry.

text: Elekere Naịjirịa anaghị agbanwe n'afọ dum. N'ọnwa Julaị, mgbe ọ bụ etiti ehihie n'Abuja, elekere ole ka ọ bụ na London?
gloss: Nigeria's clock never changes during the year. In July, when it is noon in Abuja, what time is it in London? — 12 noon: Nigeria is on UTC+1 all year, and in July Britain is on summer time, also UTC+1. 11 o'clock is the winter answer.

text: N'akụkọ mgbe ochie ndị Ijipt, kedu chi nwere isi nkịta ọhịa, onye na-eche ndị nwụrụ anwụ nche?
gloss: In ancient Egyptian myth, which god has the head of a jackal and guards the dead? — Anubis. Horus and Ra are falcon-headed, Thoth ibis-headed.
